Client-side code execution in Oculus Browser may become local OS user execution context, but CVE-2019-3562 only says code may be executed in the browser UI context.
The target's 'gain privileges' may mean SYSTEM-level escalation, but CVE-2020-1885 does not specify SYSTEM.
The victim visiting an attacker-controlled remote web page is inferred from the CVE source description and curated rule, not established as an observed environment fact.

response.reason: CVE-2019-3562's actual described effect is HTML injection into Oculus Browser UI, UI spoofing, and only 'potentially execute code'. It does not establish local unprivileged user execution context on the host OS. CVE-2020-1885 requires 'local users' on 'Windows' with affected Oculus Desktop and a hard-link-to-log vector to 'write to arbitrary files' and 'gain privileges'. The edge's bridge assumes client-side browser code execution becomes local OS user context on the same host and that the target prerequisites are met. Those assumptions are not entailed by the supplied CVE descriptions. The edge can at most be conditional, not strict-graph supported as a confirmed causal transition.
